# Respiration, spore maintenance, hatching, and decomposition

`maintenance.tsv` records actual unchanged Java maintenance calls on real placed actors.
Source twice and the bundled JAR produced identical bytes.
The fixture contains 134 cases, 291 snapshots, 882 actor views, 157 explicit calls, and nine discovered newborns.
Each actor view records the complete 154-field organism schema.
Each snapshot records all 15 World instance fields, 52 statistics fields, and 49 actual statistics getters.

## Comparison contract

The contract and row ledger were declared before Rust comparison.
Compare all scalar, effect, photo, gas, statistics, velocity, and RNG double bits exactly.
Compare endpoints, bounds, ARGB values, reactions, integer wrapping, references, and ordering exactly.
Only organism geometry fields `_m`, `_m1`, `_m2`, `_mass`, and `_I` use the existing geometry allowance.
For finite geometry, use `1e-10 * max(1, abs(expected))`.
Keep explicit NaN classification and signed infinity checks for those five fields.
Do not extend that allowance to velocities, effects, world gases, or statistics.

Every primary, infected, and saved genome reference receives an object-identity label.
Full G/N blocks retain every actual genome and gene field.
Per-Gene mutable-object alias topology remains covered by the separate genetics oracle.
This fixture does not claim another independent per-Gene identity comparison.

The Java World/VisibleWorld actor references remain two named `O` collaborator exclusions.
Four `V` fields remain named UI/corridor exclusions: `_visibleWorld`, `inCorridors`, `outCorridors`, and `_corridorexists`.
Their source observations remain available; empty corridor lists do not demonstrate Rust networking.
The setup `visible:selected` record is source callback-routing metadata.
All other recorded world state, tree membership/query behavior, actor state, statistics, and RNG remain comparison obligations.

## Execution and input authority

Compile `tools/reference/MaintenanceOracle.java` against each pinned backend.
Run `biogenesis.MaintenanceOracle NEW_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` with the isolated arguments recorded in the provenance.
The helper validates all four explicit profile roots through `toRealPath` before simulation access.
It rejects existing output directories.
Six actual negative invocations cover each omitted root, an escaped symlink, and existing output preservation.
The existing runner applies bounded execution and owned process-group cleanup.
Positive runs use a 120-second bound; negative invocations use a 30-second bound.

Each case resets actual `Utils.DEF_*` values before applying its explicit settings.
`U` records all 147 mutable primitive settings actually used by that case.
Initial organism attempts are zero; initial oxygen is `1000`.
Mutation settings are minimum `0`, maximum `10000`, and meta rate `0`.
GREEN selection weight is `7`; other selectable weights are zero.
Some payment cases explicitly change `SPORE_ENERGY_CONSUMPTION` to `2`.
No genesis or world frame executes.

Each case creates a real headless `VisibleWorld(null)` and real World.
The helper uses actual gas-add, paste, and World.addOrganism methods.
Selector, victim, and killer are pasted in that order at `(1000,1000)`, `(3500,3500)`, and `(2000,2000)`.
Their initial IDs are `0`, `1`, and `2`.
The selector is selected before the first add, avoiding MainWindow callback branches without mocks.
Creation events, population events, storage insertion, IDs, gases, and statistics remain actual source behavior.

The random seed is initially `827364`.
Labelled mobile/frozen cases reset the actual stream to seed `57` after construction.
This seed produces observable source movement and separates frozen draw retention from mobile draw consumption.
The segment vectors and masses differ, making reverse segment iteration observable.
No scripted Random outputs or copied velocity formulas supply expected results.
`R` peeks through a serialized Random copy without consuming the actual stream.

Five initial genome identities are supplied before actor construction.
`g0`, `g1`, and `g2` are explicit; `g3` and `g4` use actual GeneticCode.clone on `g0`.
Ordinary `g0` has GREEN, CYAN, and EYE genes.
`g1` and `g2` each have one GREEN gene.
Lengths are `12`, branch is `0`, and gene theta is `index * 0.25`.
The zero-mass case supplies zero lengths instead.
Symmetry is `1`; mirror, mutation rate, and activity are `0`.
All four modifiers are `1`, except the supplied spore modifier, usually `9` or `10`.
All fifteen constructor booleans are false; generation is `41` and clade is `root`.
Full `input` G/N rows retain every supplied value.

Common labelled victim controls supply energy `20`, maintenance `0.1`, age `0`, maximum age `10`, and spore version `0`.
Each scenario then supplies its named differences.
The first snapshot follows these explicitly recorded inputs.
Real paste starts growth ratio at `16`.
Adult last-birth cases supply growth ratio before actual `symmetric` and forced `calculateBounds` calls.
No helper formula constructs geometry, payment results, biological state, or statistics expectations.

## Source outcomes

| Group | Actual observations |
| --- | --- |
| Respiration | Full, partial, empty, exhausted, negative, NaN, and infinite numeric paths. |
| Age | Increment, shifted ties, strict age-out, negative age, and signed integer wrapping. |
| Excess energy | Fractional Java casts, doubled-threshold wrapping, subtraction wrapping, and guarded negative thresholds. |
| Late reproduction | Positive delay, infectious bypass, exact threshold ties, countdown clearing, and retained countdowns. |
| Dying adult spore | Modifiers 9/10, successful placement, blocked placement, oxygen-only death, integer half-threshold, and growth gating. |
| Last-birth references | Infection/saved clearing and saved-only whole-genome reuse. |
| Version dispatch | Versions `2,1,5,6,3,4,7,-3,-2,-1,0`. |
| Version ages | Different `>` and `>=` decisions at the same shifted age. |
| Injury | Partial decomposition blocks later age, movement, hatching, and timer work. |
| Mobile spores | Frozen retention, reverse iteration, velocity clamping, source RNG consumption, and zero-mass NaNs. |
| Timers/colors | Positive, zero, negative, and wrapping timers; exact CYAN, SPORE, FLOWER, and retained temporary colors. |
| Hatching | First-payment success, partial first payment, guarded fallback, partial fallback, exhaustion, and no oxygen. |
| Hatching state | Coefficients, eye rebuilding, cached endpoints, genome references, age increment, and reset-to-one callers. |
| Corpses | Actual prior death followed by full, partial, empty, negative, and NaN decomposition. |
| Version 6 photosynthesis | Eighth-frame methanotrophy, non-eighth retention, lime crowding, colony reset, and ordinary photosynthesis. |
| Version 6 reproduction | Early blond threshold, late hatching, blocked viral birth, successful viral birth, and post-birth exhaustion. |
| Newborn identity | Actual storage insertion, events, source order, signed ID wrapping, and duplicate numeric IDs. |

Breath exhaustion preserves phenotype and infection/saved references when the source avoids `die`.
Ordinary death, age-out death, and oxygen-failure death retain their separate source effects.
Only age-out reaches the adult negative-one spore's last-birth operation.
The odd reproduction threshold uses Java integer division before comparison.
Energy `50.25` passes a recorded threshold based on reproduction energy `101`; energy `50` does not.
Blocked placement produces no newborn and consumes its actual constructor/inheritance RNG draws.
Post-death observations cannot expose a discarded failed candidate's private intermediate fields.

Version 1 and version 5 use their actual separate respiration costs and movement denominators.
Version 2 and version 6 retain their different age boundary from versions 1/5.
Version 6 injury payment occurs before its age and threshold checks.
The corpus preserves exhaustion branches that report death without recoloring or clearing every reference.
Corpse decomposition changes gases and energy without delivering another death event.

Successful direct hatch increments age; several decay callers instead set age to one.
Hatching resets frame-color duration while retaining the recorded temporary color object.
The modifier 9/10 cases first invoke real blueSpore/cyanSpore, then real hatch.
The failure-after-blue-spore case retains the actual dormant state and cached data after failed payments.
Current colors, photo arrays, body arrays, flags, and bounds remain fully observed.

The controlled IEEE cases use valid placed actors with explicit raw scalar inputs.
They do not claim that the player UI accepts every supplied numeric value.
No raw-null genotype, null phenotype color, or uninitialized actor allocation occurs here.
No separate invalid-state fixture or diagnostic substitution is required.

## Newborn discovery and frozen spatial state

After each actual call, the helper scans World._organisms in its current list order.
An IdentityHashMap distinguishes newly inserted objects from previously observed actors.
It assigns `newborn0`, `newborn1`, and subsequent labels independently of numeric IDs.
The helper emits `D` only for actual inserted objects.
It then observes every original and discovered actor in every later snapshot.
Post-call D/G/N observations never become actor or genome construction inputs.

New primary, infected, or saved genome objects receive appended `gN` identities when first observed.
Shared initial genomes retain their original identities.
The saved-only last birth actually uses `g4`; other observed births can create another code identity.
The ID-wrap case inserts ID `2147483647`, then observes NEXT_ID `-2147483648`.
The duplicate-ID case actually contains IDs `0,1,2,1`, with two distinct objects labelled separately.

Frozen-tree cases call actual STRtree insertion/build methods using already recorded actors and their current bounds.
The blocker uses an explicitly supplied rectangle around the victim.
`J` records insertion membership and envelopes; `Q` records actual query result order.
Newborns remain absent from an existing frozen tree until an explicit rebuild.
The helper does not run World.time or rebuild the index implicitly after birth.

## TSV schema

Rows are tab-separated ASCII, with one newline after each row.
Doubles use sixteen hexadecimal raw IEEE digits.
Arrays and lists retain comma-separated order; empty lists have an empty final value.
Null references use `~`; object-presence observations use `present`.
The existing death schema supplies `C/U/I/A/P/K/O/H/W/S/T/G/N/R/E`.

| Added or specialized tag | Columns after the tag |
| --- | --- |
| `B` | Stage, `useDecayEnergy`, actual boolean return. |
| `D` | Stage, discovered newborn label, actual numeric ID, actual genome identity. |
| `V` | Stage, original World field, reflected Java simple type, observed value. |
| `J` | Stage, inserted actor label, rectangle X, Y, width, height. |
| `Q` | Stage, queried actor label, actual ordered hit-label CSV. |

`K` columns are stage, operation, victim role, and argument.
Operations are `breath`, `decay`, `hatch`, `useDecayEnergy`, `die`, `symmetric_bounds`, `blueSpore`, `cyanSpore`, and `build_tree`.
`useDecayEnergy` receives raw double bits.
`build_tree` receives ordered actor labels or `~` for an empty tree.
Other operations use `~`; `die` supplies a null killer.
`symmetric_bounds` invokes actual symmetric followed by calculateBounds(true).

`I` uses the existing named actor, world, statistics, and genome targets.
`rng:seed` supplies a long and resets actual Random.
The helper can represent `utils:SETTING` controls; current scenarios record their settings through `U` before construction.
Genome setup recipes remain `explicit` or `clone:g0`.
`V _organisms` uses object-identity actor labels in actual world order.
`V colDetTree` is `present,<actual size>`.
`V worldStatistics` and `V _visibleWorld` record actual object presence.
`V nFrames` has reflected type `int`; the existing `W nFrames` getter-style observation has type `long`.
The 15 World instance fields exclude static serialVersionUID.

Organism identity dispatch precedes Rectangle dispatch because Organism inherits Rectangle.
The previous serializer incorrectly emitted rectangle values for nonempty Q rows and V._organisms.
Its fixture, helper, documents, receipts, and failed consumer receipt remain archived under the original run directory.
The repair changes exactly 24 Q values and 291 V._organisms values into their actual identity labels.
Every other row remains byte-identical; case counts, ledgers, numerical results, and tolerances remain unchanged.
The provenance links the archived version and the exact row-difference receipt.

Explicit calls comprise 33 breaths, 83 decays, 11 hatches, seven decay-energy payments, and five prior deaths.
Setup calls comprise nine geometry rebuilds, six tree builds, two blue spores, and one cyan spore.
There are nine actual discovered newborns and seven actual decay-energy return observations.
Nested reproduction, gas operations, and death events remain included in the observed state and RNG.
Their internal calls are not invented additional explicit K records.

Source methods occupy `Organism.java:4570-4644`, `Organism.java:4648-4930`, and `Organism.java:5006-5045`.
World gas methods occupy `World.java:318-384`; event routing occupies `World.java:747-768`.
The provenance records actual argv, exits, versions, helper/backend hashes, equality, guards, and preserved source/fixture pins.
The original 74 files and 19 other TSV fixtures retain their recorded hashes.
The superseded maintenance fixture remains archived with its original hash.
The initial mistaken 16-field helper guard failed before output; its separate receipt remains preserved.

This fixture does not execute World.time, complete-frame scheduling, biological contacts, UI controls, or networking.
It does not accept every reproduction/transformation method or every caller's collision ordering.
It does not demonstrate save-format migration or distributable behavior.
Rust integration results remain separate from this Java observation provenance.
